title: Grade 7 Science — Fri, Jun 13
description: Fibre to Fabric — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — synthetic vs natural, properties, fabric identification
subject: science

questions.question: Which of these is a synthetic (man-made) fibre?
questions.explanation: Nylon is synthetic — made from chemicals (polyamides) in factories. Cotton, wool, and jute are natural fibres.

questions.question: What happens when a synthetic fabric like polyester is held near a flame?
options: It catches fire slowly and smells like burning hair
It melts and drips — it does not catch fire like natural fibres
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres melt near flame and can stick to skin causing burns. Natural fibres like cotton and wool char/burn cleanly.

questions.question: Which natural fibre is best for summer wear in India?
questions.explanation: Cotton absorbs sweat and allows air circulation, keeping the body cool in India's hot and humid summers.

questions.question: Which natural fibre is best for winter wear?
questions.explanation: Wool traps body heat due to its crimped structure that holds air pockets, making it ideal for cold winters.

questions.question: Rayon is a special fibre called 'artificial silk' because it:
options: Is made from silkworms in factories
Is made from cellulose (plant material) but processed chemically to look and feel like silk
Is a type of synthetic plastic
Is made from recycled cotton only
questions.explanation: Rayon is made from wood pulp cellulose that is chemically processed into silk-like threads. It is semi-synthetic.

questions.question: Which test quickly distinguishes WOOL from COTTON?
options: Burn test — wool smells like burning hair (keratin); cotton smells like burning paper (cellulose)
questions.explanation: Wool is made of keratin protein and smells like burning hair. Cotton is cellulose and smells like burning paper when burned.

questions.question: Nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre, developed in:
questions.explanation: Nylon was invented by DuPont chemists in the USA in the 1930s. It was first used for toothbrush bristles and stockings.

questions.question: An advantage of synthetic fibres over natural fibres is that they:
options: Are generally stronger, cheaper, and dry faster
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres like polyester and nylon are strong, inexpensive, resist wrinkles, and dry quickly after washing.

questions.question: A major environmental disadvantage of synthetic fibres is:
options: They are not biodegradable and release microplastics when washed
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres (plastic-based) do not biodegrade and release microplastics during washing, which pollute waterways.

questions.question: Silk is considered a luxury fibre because:
options: It is rare, labour-intensive to produce, and has a unique natural sheen and smoothness
It is only white in colour
It is produced by machines cheaply
questions.explanation: Silk production (sericulture and weaving) is slow and requires significant skill. One cocoon yields only ~600m of thread.

questions.question: A blended fabric (like polyester-cotton) combines:
options: Properties of two fibres — cotton's comfort with polyester's strength and wrinkle-resistance
Two types of natural fibres only
questions.explanation: Blended fabrics (e.g., polycotton) combine natural and synthetic fibres to get the best properties of both.

questions.question: Which of the following is a natural fibre that is also eco-friendly and biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Jute is a natural, biodegradable fibre obtained from the jute plant. It decomposes naturally, unlike synthetic fibres.

questions.question: What is the source of acrylic fibre (like in acrylic sweaters)?
questions.explanation: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre made from petroleum-based chemicals. It mimics wool's softness and warmth at lower cost.

questions.question: Which of the following matches the fibre to its source correctly?
questions.explanation: Silk comes from the Bombyx mori silkworm. Cotton → cotton plant; Wool → sheep/goat; Jute → jute plant.

questions.question: The fibre used to make durable carpets, ropes, and gunny bags — especially in West Bengal — is:
questions.explanation: Jute is a strong, coarse natural fibre used for ropes, sacks, carpets, and packaging. West Bengal and Bangladesh are major producers.
